subject: Post-call: PayGrid model-fit eval — next steps & parity thresholds
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Khan <sarah.khan@paygrid.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: PayGrid model-fit eval — next steps & parity thresholds

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary from today
- Primary goal: replace proprietary reranker for invoice-matching flows while keeping error rate within business tolerance and improving latency/cost.
- Key constraints: <10ms p50 for short queries, data residency in us-east, PII redaction required before evaluation.

Proposed next steps
1) You send a representative eval dataset (anonymized) to the Drive link below — we can accept CSV or NDJSON.
2) Redwood will run a model-fit eval (3 candidate open models + our baseline run) and share a detailed report within 5 business days of dataset receipt.
3) Define acceptance thresholds: we recommend parity target of within 3% absolute on NDCG@10 vs your proprietary baseline OR no more than 2% drop on the primary business metric you call out.
4) If parity criteria are met, we propose a canary deploy in staging with A/B for 2 weeks to validate production behavior.

Recommended candidate models (initial):
- Llama-2-13B (quantized 4-bit) — good instruction-following and reranking quality.
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (8-bit) — strong on short-context recall, lower cost.
- RedOpt-6B (Redwood-optimized quantized variant) — fast KV-cache behavior, tuned for latency.

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.csv (example prompts + labels), eval_plan_paygrid.docx (timeline + metrics).
Benchmarks & resources: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/paygrid-2026
Drive (upload dataset): https://drive.redwood.internal/paygrid/eval-dataset

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the expected SLA for the canary (p50/p95 latency targets)?
- Who should be our security/compliance contact for the SOC2/data handling checklist?

I'll coordinate with Marissa to run the technical eval once we have the dataset.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Sarah Khan <sarah.khan@paygrid.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: PayGrid model-fit eval — next steps & parity thresholds

Hi Sarah — thanks for the quick reply and for looping Security. A few notes from the eval/ML side: 

1) Data handling: masked PII is fine for our opaque eval runs; for full breakdowns we prefer tokenized hashes for fields that must remain verifiable but not reversible. If PayGrid Security requires, we can run the eval inside a customer-managed VPC (Redwood Private) — let us know.

2) Eval metrics & acceptance: we'll produce the following report fields (we'll share the template right after this email):
   - NDCG@1/5/10 (primary), MRR, Recall@K for the labeled set
   - Delta vs your proprietary baseline (absolute and relative)
   - Latency distribution (p50/p90/p95), memory footprint, and token cost per inference
   - Regression checks: we'll run our regression suite on your prompt set (prompt_set_v1.csv) and flag any categories with >2% absolute drop in F1.

3) Candidate models and rationale (short):
   - Llama-2-13B (4-bit q) — expected to match quality; watch for throughput limits on small GPU pods.
   - Mistral-7B-Instruct (8-bit) — strong cost/latency tradeoff, may slightly lag on rare-failure categories.
   - RedOpt-6B (Redwood quantized) — fastest, good baseline for canary to validate infra.

4) Acceptance thresholds suggestion (for discussion):
   - Quality parity: NDCG@10 within 3% absolute OR no >2% absolute drop on your primary business metric.
   - Latency: p50 within 1.2x of baseline, p95 no more than 1.5x during canary.

5) Timeline: once we have the dataset (T0), our standard schedule is:
   - T0+2 business days: internal eval report + topline findings
   - T0+5 business days: full report with breakdowns + recommended canary config

Attaching an internal summary of early evals we've run on a public proxy dataset so you have an idea of expected deltas (eval_results_summary.pdf).

Let us know the Drive path once uploaded. We'll provision a dedicated eval runner scoped to your dataset and model candidates.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
